info.description:
Everything is under `/v1`. **The server enforces; a client only offers**: a permission, an ETag, a name and a form are all checked again here, whatever a screen showed.

A write is conditional (`If-None-Match: *` creates, `If-Match` replaces or deletes; 428 otherwise) and every error is RFC 9457 problem details with the form field of every 422. Every answer is `Cache-Control: no-store`.

**Reading this document.** `x-permission` on an operation is the one permission the route needs (a value of the token's roles claim, e.g. `platform:agents.read`); `null` means any valid token. `x-secrets-pick` is present on a write whose body can name a Secret key: such a write needs that permission as well, and is a 403 naming it without it. **Problems** (`application/problem+json`): `type` is `urn:vymalo:agents:problem:<slug>` and the table `x-problem-table` of this `info` object lists every slug with its status and meaning; a path that is no route is 404 `no-such-route` and a method a path does not serve is 405 `method-not-allowed` with an `Allow` header, both answered before a token is asked for, on every path below. **Base URL:** the deployment's public address of this API (the chart's Ingress host), which a client is configured with; the paths here are under `/v1` and relative to it.

**Deliberately absent:** cookies and sessions (the token is the only credential); CORS credentials (`Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` is never sent) and a wildcard origin (only the deployment's exact origins are allowed); an unconditional write or delete; a secret value anywhere (a form names a Secret key, and the API reads no Secret); DPoP.

This document is generated from the API's table of routes and held equal to the checked-in `docs/api/platform-api-v1.openapi.json` by a test.

The object is being deleted: the operator has not finished. Read again later.
Another manager owns a field of the object (a server-side apply conflict).

get.description: Why is it not `Ready`: the Kubernetes Events (core/v1) about the agent's `AgentService`, its `AgentConfig` and what the operator made for it, **newest first, at most 100**. **Attributed by the names the operator gives an agent's objects** (`by: name`; the agent's own `AgentService` and `AgentConfig` by uid, `by: uid`): the workloads `<agent>`, `<agent>-front` and `<agent>-egress`, their ReplicaSets and pods, and the store's `<agent>-db` cluster, pods, jobs and services. An event of another agent's object never appears, and one whose name could be two agents' is left out; **an unrelated object of the namespace whose name has the same shape can appear**. Not covered: volume claims and the pods a coder makes for its runs. A 404 `not-found` (the same body as `GET /v1/agents/{name}`) for an agent that is not there. **Kubernetes keeps events for a limited time** (the API server's `--event-ttl`, one hour by default: *verified 2026-11-14* in the API server's source), so an empty list does not mean healthy; `incomplete: true` says the list may be missing events (tell the person). **The messages are the cluster's words**: untrusted text, render it as text; cleaned of control and bidirectional characters and cut (see `AgentEvent.message`); never logged.
